title: Bijectivity of the normalized affine resolution section class
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes, $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, $I$ an injective resolution of $F$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], $p\in\mathbb N$, and $V\subset S$ an affine open. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $M=F|_U$ and $P=R^p f_*F$, where cohomology and ordinary higher images are right derived functors [pqf-def-cohomology]. Let $R$ be any augmentation-preserving restricted resolution section data [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Then the specified additive class map $c:H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,M)\to\Gamma(V,P)$ is bijective, where $c$ is resolutionSectionClass for $R$, followed by evaluation at $V$ of the inverse of $I.\mathrm{isoRightDerivedObj}(f_*,p)$. The class map sends the cohomology class of a cocycle of the restricted resolution to the section of the homology sheaf it defines [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. No Ext comparison is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tags 01F4 (2), 01XJ (1), 01E4 and 01E5; affine degeneration and normalization on cocycles

proof.text: Set U=f inverse V, g=f restricted to U -> V, and M=F restricted to U. Restriction preserves quasi-coherence; g is qcqs by base change. Its higher images are quasi-coherent. On affine V their positive cohomology vanishes, so the cocycle-defined Leray edge is an isomorphism in degree p. Open restriction and restrictAppIso identify its target with Gamma(V,R^p f_*F).

Choose a global-section cocycle representing a class computed by R.resolution. R.components identifies its representative with the original resolution evaluated on U; R.augmentation says the comparison induces the identity on M. Independence and naturality of injective-resolution computations therefore identify the two cohomology classes. The Leray cocycle formula projects this representative to the homology sheaf of f_*I. By the cohomology-presheaf description this is precisely the homology evaluation comparison followed by sectionCohomologyTheta, and then the inverse resolution comparison. This is c. The edge and all the comparisons are isomorphisms, hence c is bijective. In degree zero the same computation uses the augmentation. Empty V and zero F yield zero groups.
